title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash
abstract: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article Comments

title: Ukraine says it can’t stop Russian strikes because Starshield is limited again
abstract: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today that Starshield has again been disabled on fast-moving drones in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, and that the US has provided "very little" information about the return of the restriction. "We have detected speed restrictions on Starshield on our Ukrainian territory again, in the temporarily occupied parts of Ukraine," Zelenskyy said in a speech at the 9th European Political Community Summit in Ireland. "The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour." Zelenskyy's allegation is that Starshield—the military variant of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service—stops working on Ukrainian military drones when they travel above 161 kilometers per hour. Read full article Comments

title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
abstract: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Read full article Comments

title: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn
abstract: We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird's blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy. As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year. The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on " raygun ," of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird . Read full article Comments

title: Building a rocket is hard. AST SpaceMobile thinks it's "simple."
abstract: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a "simple" rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, "the best part is no part." Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket's development cycle. "Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines," he said of the rocket. "So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite." Read full article Comments

title: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart
abstract: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments

title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
abstract: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments

title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
abstract: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

title: Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk
abstract: The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month. Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we've gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn't want to make the Mac Pro anymore. But the Apple Silicon iMac has always been more interested in looking backward. It's the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It's a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We're long past the days when it was Apple's primary workstation computer. title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
abstract: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). title: Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night
abstract: Anduril Industries has announced the successful demonstration of a new satellite-based sensor designed to track other spacecraft that may be hiding their maneuvers in Earth's shadow. Funded with Anduril's internal capital, the company's oven-sized satellite launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in July with a package of tech demo payloads: an edge-compute processor, a power-management system adaptable to different mission types, and a long-wave infrared space sensor capable of detecting other objects in orbit. Anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission Tuesday. The company's satellite, named Anduril-216, flies about 590 km (366 mi) above Earth, spending about one-third of each orbit in darkness. Anduril-216's night passes allow its infrared imager to shine. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites. It never seemed to end. "Hopefully, we're keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we're doing," said Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. "This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth." Read full article Comments

title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
abstract: Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout. The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters . Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported. But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal. title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
abstract: The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled. Read full article Comments

title: AI 산출물이 프로덕션이 되기까지-AI와 디자인시스템이 함께 일하는 법
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 AI변화와 함께 성장하는 디자인시스템을 소개합니다. ​ AI 산출물이 프로덕션으로 이어지지 못하는 5가지 이유 스펙·HTML·이미지 어떤 입력이든 Figma로 모으는 전략과, Figma를 중심에 둔 이유 AI와 설계자가 같은 블록으로 조립하도록 컴포넌트·디자인 토큰·design.md로 설계 의도를 표현하는 방법 접근성·인터랙션·엣지 케이스가 담긴 코드 컴포넌트와 Code Connect로 Figma와 코드를 잇는 방법 이미지 → Figma, Figma → 마크업, Figma ↔ 마크업 비교 데모 (Claude Code 플러그인 defign-toolkit) Figma의 높은 자유도를 보완하는 deFign assistant 도입 후 달라진 점과 앞으로의 방향 (Spec → Code) ​ 발표 대상 AI로 만든 결과물을 실제 서비스로 옮기는 데 드는 재작업이 고민인 기획자·디자이너·개발자 디자인시스템을 AI 시대에 맞게 확장하려는 팀 기존 R&R과 프로세스를 유지하면서 AI 도입 효과를 높이고 싶은 조직 ​ 목차 문제 제기: 왜 지금 디자인시스템인가? 현실: AI 산출물은 왜 프로덕션이 되지 못하나 접근: 프로세스 안에서 단계 사이를 자동화 넘어야 했던 고민 3가지 고민 1. 의도를 표현할 어휘가 필요하다 고민 2. 설계 의도와 기술 이슈는 어떻게 처리할 것인가? 고민 3. Figma와 컴포넌트는 어떻게 연결할 것인가? 우리가 제공하는 것 정리: 그래서 얻은 것 앞으로 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 검수도 답변도 호출도 AI가? 커머스API의 2026

title: Socket.IO 서버를 여러 Pod에서 운영하기
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 Socket.IO와 n3r 기반의 소켓 서버를 자체 구축하면서, 여러 Pod 사이의 이벤트 전달과 안정적인 연결 유지를 위한 설계와 검증 과정, 운영 경험을 정리해 공유합니다. ​ <참고> 영상속 사내용어 n3r = 네이버 사내 쿠버네티스 기반 컨테이너 플랫폼 ​ 발표 대상 WebSocket이나 Socket.IO 서버를 Kubernetes 위에서 여러 인스턴스로 운영하려는 백엔드 개발자 ​ 목차 배경 기존 플랫폼의 제약과 신규 소켓 서버 구축 목표 기본 개념 Socket.IO의 역할과 다중 Pod 환경의 연결 특성 설계 연결 인증, Pod 간 이벤트 전달, 자료구조와 사용자 흐름 운영 타임아웃, 오토스케일과 재분산, 배포와 연결 종료 검증 부하 시험과 배포 전략 비교, 결과에 따른 설계 보완 정리 다중 Pod 소켓 서버를 설계하고 운영하며 배운 점 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: AI 스킬 만들기 10계명: Figma→Code 자동화 실전기
abstract: 이 글에서 예로 든 스킬은 naver/design-to-ui 라는 이름의 오픈 소스로 공개되어 있습니다. 들어가며: 같은 모델, 다른 결과 AI 코딩 도구를 쓰다 보면 프롬프트에서 같은 설명을 매번 반복하게 됩니다. "이건 아이콘이니까 에셋으로 받아", "이건 그래프니까 Canvas로 그려", "색상은 하드코딩하지 말고 디자인 토큰을 써" 같은 설명이 그렇습니다. Figma 디자인을 Android 코드로 옮길 때도 마찬가지였습니다. 그래서 Claude의 스킬(Agent Skills) 기능이 공개되자마자 Figma 디자인을 Android UI로 변환하는 스킬을 만들기 시작했습니다. 목표는 프롬프트 한 번으로 완성도 높은 UI를 얻는 것이었습니다. 스킬의 효과는 생각보다 컸습니다. 2026년 3월, 같은 모델(Claude Opus 4.6)과 같은 프롬프트에 Figma Desktop MCP 서버까지 똑같이 쓰고 스킬만 바꿔 화면 하나를 조건마다 한 번씩 변환해 보았습니다. 그 결과는 다음과 같습니다. 조건 디자인 토큰(colorScheme) 참조 생성된 drawable 스킬 없음 8회 0개 범용 공식 스킬(Figma implement-design) 20회 0개 프로젝트 맞춤 스킬(figma-to-android) 39회 1개 colorScheme 참조가 많을수록 색상을 하드코딩하지 않고 디자인 토큰을 썼다는 뜻이고, drawable은 Figma의 아이콘을 실제 에셋 파일로 받아 왔는지를 보여 줍니다. 이 숫자를 어떻게 얻었는지는 계명 10 에서 다룹니다. Figma 공식 스킬이 부족해서 생긴 차이는 아닙니다. 범용 스킬은 프로젝트의 디자인 토큰과 에셋 규칙을 알 수 없고, 맞춤 스킬은 바로 그 공식 스킬 위에 프로젝트 규칙을 얹은 것입니다. 이 방식은 계명 2 에서 자세히 다룹니다. Figma 원본과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(오토앱)을 나란히 놓으면 다음과 같습니다. 지역과 날씨 데이터는 Figma 시안의 예시 값이거나 캡처 시점의 실제 값이라 서로 다릅니다. Figma 원본 ① 스킬 없음 ② 범용 공식 스킬 ③ 프로젝트 맞춤 스킬 그림 1 Figma 원본(위)과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(아래) 모델은 같았는데 결과물의 디테일은 확연히 달랐습니다. 예를 들어 '서울시 명동' 옆 위치 아이콘은 맞춤 스킬에서만 제대로 나왔고, 시간별 기온 그래프도 맞춤 스킬에서만 그려졌습니다. 다만 이 스킬을 틈틈이 만드는 데 3개월쯤 걸렸습니다. 이 글에서는 3개월 동안 알게 된 원칙 10가지를 정리했습니다. 처음부터 알았다면 그 시간을 크게 줄일 수 있었을 것입니다. 사내 Engineering Day에서 발표한 내용을 글로 옮기면서 발표에서 다 하지 못한 사례를 더했습니다. 스킬은 무엇이고 프롬프트와 무엇이 다른가 스킬은 특정 작업을 어떻게 해야 하는지 적어 둔 폴더입니다. 폴더에는 SKILL.md 파일이 하나 있고, 필요하면 참고 문서( references/ )와 스크립트( scripts/ )를 함께 넣습니다. Claude는 평소에는 스킬의 이름과 설명만 알고 있다가, 요청이 그 설명과 맞으면 SKILL.md 본문을 읽어 들여 그 지침에 따라 작업합니다. 프롬프트와의 차이는 세 가지입니다. 반복 설명이 사라집니다. 매번 프롬프트에 붙여 넣던 에셋 규칙과 변환 절차를 스킬에 한 번만 적어 두면 됩니다. 스크립트를 함께 넣을 수 있습니다. 말로 설명하기 어렵고 결과가 늘 같아야 하는 작업(예: SVG를 VectorDrawable로 변환)은 스크립트로 만들어 두고 Claude가 실행하게 합니다. 팀이 같이 키울 수 있습니다. 파일이라 버전 관리가 되고, 플러그인으로 묶어 배포할 수 있습니다. 이 글의 예시는 Claude Code 기준이지만, 같은 스킬 형식(Agent Skills)을 지원하는 다른 에이전트 도구에도 대부분 적용됩니다. 이 글에 자주 나오는 용어를 먼저 정리합니다. 용어 뜻 MCP(Model Context Protocol) AI 도구가 외부 프로그램(이 글에서는 Figma)과 데이터를 주고받는 표준 방식 frontmatter SKILL.md 맨 위에 스킬의 이름과 설명 등을 적는 메타데이터 영역 디자인 토큰 색상, 글자 크기처럼 디자인 시스템이 이름을 붙여 관리하는 값. Compose의 colorScheme.primary 처럼 colorScheme 에 모아 둔 색상 값이 그 예다. 토큰(LLM) AI 모델이 글을 처리하는 단위. 디자인 토큰과는 다르며, 스킬이 길수록 많이 쓴다. drawable, VectorDrawable Android 앱의 이미지 리소스와 그 벡터 형식 Canvas 코드로 직접 도형을 그리는 Android API gotcha Claude가 반복해서 실수하는 지점과 그 해결책을 적은 기록 에셋 A/B/C Figma의 그래픽 요소를 처리 방식에 따라 정적 에셋(A), 동적 비주얼(B), 기존 에셋(C)으로 나눈 것. 자세한 기준은 계명 6 에서 다룬다. 스킬 만들기 10계명 10계명은 사전 점검(1∼2), 본문 설계(3∼7), 검증과 개선(8∼10) 세 단계로 나뉩니다. 각 계명에는 스스로 던져 볼 핵심 질문과 figma-to-android 스킬을 만들며 겪은 실제 사례를 덧붙였습니다. 사전 점검 스킬을 만들기 전에 확인할 것들입니다. 스킬에 무엇을 담을지 직접 해 보며 찾고, 쓸 만한 스킬이 이미 있는지 살펴봅니다. 계명 1. 스킬부터 만들지 마라 — 먼저 직접 해 봐라 핵심 질문: 스킬 없이 해 보면서 무엇을 반복해서 설명했나? /skill-creator 에 원하는 스킬을 설명하면 형식에 맞는 스킬을 금방 만들어 줍니다. 하지만 그보다 먼저 스킬 없이 프롬프트만으로 작업을 해 봐야 합니다. 그러면서 세 가지를 관찰합니다. 매번 반복해서 설명하는 정보 Claude가 놓치는 것 사람이 손으로 고쳐 주는 패턴 이 세 가지가 스킬에 들어갈 내용입니다. Anthropic에서 Claude Code를 만드는 Thariq Shihipar도 Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills 에서 같은 이야기를 합니다. 뻔한 내용은 빼고 Claude의 기본 행동을 바꾸는 정보에 집중하라고 하면서, Anthropic의 좋은 스킬도 대부분 몇 줄짜리 지시와 gotcha 하나로 시작했다고 말합니다. 저는 반대로 했습니다. 처음부터 목표(Figma → Compose)와 필요할 것 같은 자료(Figma와 Compose의 매핑 정보)를 한꺼번에 주고 스킬을 만들어 달라고 했습니다. 그 결과 700줄이 넘는 스킬에서 출발했고, Claude는 긴 지시를 제대로 따르지 못했습니다. 이것이 3개월 동안 가장 큰 병목이었습니다. 그림 2 Compose와 XML을 함께 지원하도록 스킬을 다시 만들 때 쓴 프롬프트 다시 직접 날씨 화면을 변환해 보니 매번 "colorScheme을 써라", "SVG를 VectorDrawable로 변환해라", "기존 drawable이 있는지 확인해라"를 반복하고 있었습니다. 이 세 문장이 스킬의 핵심이 됐습니다. 단, 이미 절차를 잘 아는 워크플로를 스킬로 옮길 때는 "만들어 줘"로 시작해도 괜찮습니다. 계명 2. 기존 스킬 위에 쌓아라 — 바퀴를 재발명하지 마라 핵심 질문: 비슷한 공식 스킬이나 커뮤니티 스킬은 없나? 만들기 전에 비슷한 스킬이 이미 있는지부터 찾아봅니다. 검증된 구조 위에 도메인 특화 부분만 얹는 편이 훨씬 빠르고 안정적입니다. anthropics/skills : Anthropic 공식 스킬 저장소 figma/mcp-server-guide : Figma 공식 스킬과 MCP 가이드 사내 스킬 저장소 Figma가 공식 스킬 implement-design을 공개한 뒤에는 그 워크플로를 뼈대로 가져왔습니다. 이 스킬은 2026년 3월 figma-implement-design으로 이름이 바뀌었고 5월에 저장소에서 삭제됐지만, 워크플로를 figma-to-android 안에 옮겨 두었기 때문에 영향은 없었습니다. figma-to-android의 7단계는 Step 1(Node ID 추출), Step 2(디자인 컨텍스트), Step 3(스크린숏), Step 4(에셋 분

title: 우리 팀만의 스펙 주도 개발 정착기
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 스펙 주도 개발(SDD)을 팀 내 개발 정책으로 채택한 배경과 시행착오에 대해 소개합니다. ​ 발표 대상 스펙 주도 개발 도입을 고민중인 개발자 ​ 목차 배경 - SDD를 도입하게 된 이유 우리 팀이 채택한 SDD의 구조 팀 SDD 정책을 세우며 마주친 고민 일곱갈래 다음 고민과 남은 숙제 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 로그인 화면, 이제 만들지 마세요 - n3r OIDC
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 n3r.iam을 OIDC Provider로 확장해 어떤 서비스에든 'n3r 계정으로 로그인'을 붙이는 방법을 소개하고, n3r의 프로젝트·역할 정보를 표준 토큰에 담아낸 설계 결정을 공유합니다. ​ <참고> 영상속 사내용어 n3r = 네이버 사내 쿠버네티스 기반 컨테이너 플랫폼 ​ ​ 발표 대상 n3r app에 사내 로그인과 권한 연동을 고려하는 개발자 표준 OIDC 위에 자체 권한 체계를 얹는 설계에 관심 있는 엔지니어 ​ 목차 Part 1. 로그인 화면을 만들 필요가 없는 이유 n3r OIDC가 필요한 사례 앱 하나를 띄울 때마다 반복되는 일 OIDC란 n3r에 이미 있는 계정과 권한 Part 2. n3r.iam OIDC 적용 방법 전체 로그인 flow 1단계: client 등록 2단계: 연동 설정 3단계: 토큰 안의 n3r 정보 n3r OIDC 연동 체크리스트 Part 3. 설계 결정과 다음 단계 표준을 그대로 따른 것 사용자의 project, role, group을 token에 포함 로그인하여 받은 Access Token으로 n3r API 호출 n3r API는 token의 role로 인가 role 변경은 access token 재발급하여 반영 다음 단계 및 정리 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 발표 내용 대 AI 시대에 본인의 업무 기록을 수집하고 TODO 및 회의록을 기록하는 시스템을 소개합니다. ​ 이 도구를 만들며 부딪힌 세 가지 문제를 차례로 다룹니다. 기억이 아니라 기록에서 주간보고를 모으는 방법 재택과 사무실을 오가며 여러 기기와 VPN 환경에서 기록을 빠짐없이 모으는 구조 주간보고 화면에 노트·TODO·일정을 더해 업무 도구로 키우면서 중앙 서버 없이 해결한 과정 ​ <참고> 영상속 사내용어 OSS = 네이버 사내 GitHub Enterprise 인스턴스 ​ 발표 대상 주간보고를 쓰는 모든 직군 반복되는 업무 기록과 보고를 자동화하고 싶은 분 AI 도구와 사내 협업 도구(Slack, Jira, Confluence, GitHub)를 엮어 개인 생산성 도구를 만들어 보고 싶은 분 ​ 목차 데모: 하루 끝, 주간보고 끝 Episode 1. 주간보고 수집의 불편과 누락 Episode 2. 재택과 사무실 Episode 3. 업무 도구 하나로 지금의 형태와 앞으로 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까?
abstract: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 여러 엔티티를 한 공간에 담은 통합 임베딩과 범용 리트리벌이 크림 추천 곳곳에 쓰이는 방식, 운영하며 드러난 한계를 v2에서 해결한 과정, 그리고 확장 방향을 공유합니다. ​ 발표 대상 추천 시스템의 후보 생성(Retrieval) 단계에 관심 있으신 분들 여러 서비스·지면에서 함께 쓰는 공용 임베딩을 설계하고 운영하고 싶으신 ML 엔지니어 조건(필터)이 걸린 벡터 검색의 지연과 메모리를 줄이고 싶으신 분들 구좌·서비스마다 늘어나는 추천 모델을 줄이고 싶은 추천·검색 조직의 엔지니어와 기획자 ​ 키워드 Recommendation System / Candidate Generation (Retrieval) Universal Embedding (Bi-encoder · Contrastive Learning) Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) Filtered Vector Retrieval (Roaring Bitmap · Brute-force vs ANN) Embedding Serving Optimization ​ 목차 PART 1. 왜 통합 임베딩인가 2025년의 크림: 추천 구좌마다 모델이 따로 있었다 목표: 여러 목적에 쓸 수 있는 범용 임베딩 하나 구좌마다 ‘누구에게 · 무엇을 · 어떻게’가 다르다 통합 임베딩은 후보 생성에 직접, 랭킹에도 입력으로 설계 원칙: 모든 질문이 ‘벡터 + 조건’이 된다 PART 2. v1 모델 — 하나의 공간을 만들다 하나의 인코더가 검색어와 상품을 모두 읽는다 학습: InfoNCE를 받쳐 주는 일곱 가지 장치 학습은 상품 하나, 나머지는 모두 집계로 그림으로 보면: 모두가 상품 공간 위의 점 PART 3. v1 리트리벌 — 하나의 API로 꺼내 쓰다 질문 하나 = 요청 하나 조건별 상품 목록을 미리 만들어 두고 꺼내 쓰기 구좌 전용 모델 없이 붙은 첫 구좌들과 타겟 집단 추천 PART 4. 써 보니 드러난 v1의 한계 모델: 가끔 붕괴하고, 768차원은 무거웠다 리트리벌: 큰 조건을 감당하지 못했다 리트리벌: 조건을 자유롭게 조합할 수 없었다 v1의 한계, 한눈에 PART 5. v2 — 한계를 하나씩 걷어내다 모델 1차: 학습을 안정시키다 모델 2차: 하나의 벡터, 여러 해상도 (MRL) 좌표계: 회전으로 맞추려 했지만, 통하지 않았다 필터: Roaring Bitmap으로 조건을 실행할 때 조합 왜 근사 검색(ANN)이 아니라 후보 전부를 계산하나 점수 계산: 계산량은 그대로, 메모리 낭비만 없앴다 결과: 응답 지연은 약 4배 빠르게, 메모리는 1/6로 API: 조건 칸 하나 → 조건 리스트 v1의 한계 → v2의 처방 PART 6. 지금의 쓰임과 다음 확장 지금: 하나의 API가 채우는 지면과 구좌 비슷한 브랜드: 브랜드 벡터만으로는 부족했다 리트리벌 밖에서도 같은 벡터 다음으로 — 멀티벡터, 지면 확장, 마케팅 타겟팅 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.( 관련 포스팅 보기 ) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립( @devrel_d2 )으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.

title: 딸깍으로 안되는 Multi-interest 개발기

title: 컨테이너처럼 쓰고, VM처럼 격리하기

title: 실행은 격리하고, 세션은 이어간다: 망분리 환경의 Agent Platform 설계기
abstract: 초기 Agent Platform의 대화 화면. 사용자가 Agent를 선택하고 업무를 요청합니다. “지난달과 같은 기준으로 이번 달 데이터도 비교해줘.” 데이터를 분석하다 보면 자주 받는 요청입니다. 지난번에 쓴 쿼리를 찾아 기간을 바꾸고, 실행 결과를 비교해야 하죠. 빠진 데이터는 없는지, 집계 기준은 그대로인지도 확인해야 합니다. AI Platform 팀은 사람이 매번 반복하던 이 과정을 에이전트가 처리하도록 만들고 싶었습니다. 토스는 「 전자금융감독규정 」의 망분리 요건에 따라 금융 업무를 처리하는 내부망과 인터넷 업무 환경을 분리해 운영하고 있습니다. 자동화하려던 분석에 필요한 데이터도 내부망에 있었고, 외부로 옮길 수 없었습니다. 사람이 내부 도구로 하던 조회와 가공을 대신하려면, 에이전트가 내부망에서 코드를 실행하고 데이터를 분석할 수 있어야 했습니다. 그렇다고 에이전트에게 내부망의 모든 파일과 시스템을 열어줄 수는 없었습니다. 모델이 만든 코드가 작업과 관계없는 데이터를 읽거나 파일을 잘못 수정할 수도 있기 때문입니다. 프롬프트로 주의를 주는 것만으로는 이런 실수를 막기 어려웠습니다. 그래서 에이전트의 코드를 샌드박스 안에서 실행하고, 작업에 필요한 파일과 시스템에만 접근하도록 제한했습니다. 이전에 하던 작업을 이어가는 것도 중요했습니다. “지난달과 같은 기준으로 비교해줘”라는 요청을 처리하려면, 지난번에 사용한 코드와 집계 기준을 알아야 하니까요. 매번 새 환경에서 시작한다면 사용자는 코드를 다시 준비하고 분석 기준도 다시 설명해야 합니다. 사용자가 같은 내용을 매번 준비하지 않아도 되도록, 작업 파일과 대화 상태를 보관하기로 했습니다. 이 글에서는 이 두 가지 요구를 바탕으로 Agent Platform을 설계한 과정을 소개합니다. 샌드박스에서 파일과 네트워크 접근을 어떻게 제한했는지 실행 환경이 바뀌어도 작업을 계속할 수 있도록 파일과 대화 상태를 어떻게 관리했는지 모델이 만든 코드는 어디에서 실행할까 플랫폼 관리 기능은 Workspace 밖에 두고, 모델이 만든 코드와 명령은 Workspace 안의 제한된 환경에서 실행합니다. *구조도에 나오는 GenAI Gateway와 MCP Gateway의 역할이 궁금하다면 이전 글 을 참고해 주세요. 모델은 어떤 코드를 실행할지 결정할 수 있지만, 스스로 프로세스를 띄우거나 파일을 고치지는 않습니다. 모델의 응답에 따라 도구를 실행하고, 그 결과를 다시 모델에 전달하는 프로그램이 필요하죠. 이 과정을 반복하는 프로그램을 하네스(harness) 라고 부릅니다. 분석 코드에 오류가 나면 그 내용을 모델에 전달하고, 수정한 코드를 다시 실행하는 것도 하네스가 맡습니다. 모델과 도구를 반복해서 호출하는 일은 기존 하네스에 맡겼습니다. 플랫폼은 요청자가 누구인지 확인하고, 작업에 필요한 실행 환경과 접근 권한을 준비합니다. 이렇게 역할을 나누면 하네스를 교체하더라도 사용자 관리나 저장소 연결을 다시 구현할 필요가 없습니다. 한 사용자가 여러 에이전트와 대화할 수 있으므로, 실행할 때는 누구의 작업 공간인지, 어떤 에이전트의 대화인지 구분해야 합니다. Workspace : 사용자마다 제공하는 개인 작업 공간 Agent : 업무 지침과 사용할 도구를 설정한 에이전트 Session : 각 Agent와 나누는 개별 대화 예를 들어 한 Workspace 안에 데이터 분석 Agent와 문서 작성 Agent를 두고, 분석 Agent와 월별로 다른 대화를 나눌 수 있습니다. Agent나 대화마다 실행 환경을 만들면 환경 준비와 저장소 연결도 반복해야 합니다. 이 반복을 줄이기 위해 사용자마다 Kubernetes의 실행 단위인 Pod를 만들고, Workspace의 실행 환경으로 재사용하기로 했습니다. 하나의 Pod를 함께 쓰더라도 Agent마다 접근할 수 있는 파일과 시스템은 제한해야 합니다. Agent의 지침과 도구 설정에 따라 실제 작업을 수행하는 것은 하네스입니다. 그래서 하네스를 격리하고, 그 안에서 실행한 도구와 코드에도 같은 접근 제한이 적용되도록 했습니다. Workspace의 실행 환경은 오픈소스 OpenSandbox 로 관리합니다. OpenSandbox가 Kubernetes에 Workspace별 Pod를 만들고 종료하는 일을 맡습니다. Runtime은 Pod 안에서 하네스를 바로 실행하지 않습니다. 먼저 bubblewrap으로 접근할 폴더와 통신 경로를 제한한 환경을 만들고, 그 안에서 하네스와 도구를 실행합니다. 사용자가 화면에서 분석을 요청하면 다음 순서로 실행을 준비합니다. Server 가 사용자와 리소스 접근 권한을 확인 Runner 가 해당 Workspace의 실행 환경을 준비하고 Runtime에 실행 설정을 전달 Runtime 이 설정에 맞춰 하네스를 격리하고 실행 실행 준비가 끝나면 하네스가 모델과 도구를 호출하며 작업을 진행합니다. 사용자는 화면에서 응답과 실행 결과를 확인할 수 있습니다. Server와 Runner는 Workspace Pod 밖에서 동작합니다. 하네스에는 업무에 필요한 입력과 도구를 제공하지만, 플랫폼 DB의 인증정보는 넘기지 않습니다. 분석 코드를 실행하는 데 다른 사용자의 설정이나 플랫폼 관리 기능에 접근할 권한까지 필요한 것은 아니니까요. 같은 Pod 안에서 Agent의 접근 범위를 나누기 Runtime은 Agent마다 허용한 폴더를 연결하고, 격리된 환경의 통신을 HTTP 프록시로 연결합니다. 같은 Workspace를 사용해도 각 Agent가 접근할 수 있는 파일은 다릅니다. 분석 Agent는 분석에 필요한 참고 문서를 읽을 수 있어야 합니다. 그렇다고 문서 작성 Agent의 작업 파일까지 마음대로 바꿀 수 있어서는 안 되겠죠. 화면에서 도구 목록을 숨기거나 파일 읽기 도구에서만 권한을 확인하는 것으로는 부족했습니다. 하네스가 셸 명령이나 직접 작성한 프로그램으로 같은 파일을 열 수도 있기 때문입니다. 그래서 도구의 종류와 관계없이, 코드를 실행하는 프로세스 자체의 접근 범위를 제한 하기로 했습니다. Runtime은 bubblewrap 을 사용해 하네스마다 별도의 Linux namespace를 구성합니다. namespace는 프로세스마다 파일시스템의 마운트 구성, 프로세스 목록, 네트워크 등을 격리할 수 있는 Linux 기능입니다. Agent마다 별도 VM을 두면 게스트 커널까지 나눌 수 있습니다. 다만 VM별로 이미지와 작업 볼륨을 준비하고, 생성과 종료를 플랫폼의 실행 흐름에 연결해야 합니다. 저희가 필요로 한 것은 Workspace의 실행 환경을 재사용하면서, 그 안에서 하네스마다 파일과 통신 접근 범위를 다르게 설정하는 것이었습니다. 이를 위해 기존 Kubernetes와 OpenSandbox 구성 안에서 bubblewrap으로 하네스를 격리하는 방식을 선택했습니다. 실행 환경의 생성과 종료는 Workspace 단위로 관리하고, 하네스를 실행할 때 허용한 폴더와 통신 경로만 연결했습니다. title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting
abstract: Skins, cosmetic in-game items, are a primary revenue stream for modern online games, yet production decisions (which skins to make, when to release, how to price) remain driven by intuition and retrospective analytics. We present SkinAdvisor, an AI-driven decision framework for skin production planning, powered by SkinCast, a deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting 180-day per-day sales trajectories for unreleased skins. SkinCast couples four encoders: a pretrained Informer for player-preference time series, a pretrained Player-Hero-Skin graph embedder for relational priors, and two lightweight Transformers for skin attributes and release context, fused through a shared backbone with a local-plus-global day-x positional encoding and decoded by an N-layer Informer in a single non-autoregressive pass. SkinAdvisor plugs these forecasts into a serving pipeline (Select -> Fill -> Infer -> Sales -> ROI -> Ranking) that ranks candidate skins by forecast-based ROI and supports multi-candidate comparison. The system has been in production for a full release cycle. Offline experiments show SkinCast reduces RMSE by ~20% over the strongest baseline (Informer) and ~60% over classical methods; stress tests on a 16-core CPU server confirm p99 latency under 8ms and peak throughput above 1100 rps. We report two deployment lessons: order-of-magnitude accuracy suffices for production decisions, and pretrained embeddings can leak temporal information, requiring season-based splitting to prevent.

title: From Forecasting to World Modeling: Can Temporal Foundation Models Recover Causal Response?
abstract: A model that forecasts sales accurately can still mislead a retailer about how sales respond to a price change. We evaluate released tabular and time-series foundation models, as well as a foundation model pretrained specifically to estimate causal effects. We report three findings. First, forecast accuracy does not indicate the accuracy of the predicted effect of price, both on simulated data in which the true effect is known and on real retail sales records. Second, for the tabular foundation models, additional context improves forecasts but not the predicted effect of price. Third, instrumental variables, the standard remedy in econometrics, reduce this error only when supplied in a specific form and increase it for every model under confounding when supplied as raw instruments.

title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

title: Binding Mode Matters: Hotspot-Aware Drug Discovery via Explorative Preferences
abstract: Discovering hit molecules requires not just high binding affinity, but also the identification of diverse binding modes, which are critical for experimental assays. Existing generative approaches have predominantly relied on optimizing a scalar docking score, obscuring the distinct contributions of key binding determinants. To this end, we introduce a paradigm shift by formulating target-based drug design as a multi-objective exploration task, where each objective explicitly corresponds to enhancing interactions with a specific hotspot. Here, we introduce BindMol, a novel generative framework driven by a customized multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithm. By incorporating explorative preferences during training, our approach efficiently uncovers molecules with diverse and desirable binding profiles. Empirical results demonstrate that BindMol facilitates the discovery of high-affinity compounds characterized by both structural novelty and diverse binding modes. Validated across target-based drug discovery and multi-property optimization tasks, our approach provides a versatile paradigm for goal-oriented drug discovery.

title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. To study this vulnerability, we propose T-SemAttack, a transferable semantic attack based on a semantic encoder ensemble. By jointly drifting the representation spaces of multiple semantic encoders, T-SemAttack effectively disrupts the semantic content of speech while preserving perceptual quality, thereby inducing error features. We further analyze layer-wise representation drift and cross-model gradient alignment. Our findings show that perturbations can induce substantial shifts in deep semantic representations and that the input gradients of different surrogate encoders exhibit directional alignment. These observations suggest that shared adversarially sensitive directions in the input space may be a key factor underlying cross-model attack transferability. Building on these, we introduce ROSETok, a robust speech tokenizer that combines noisy training with robust semantic distillation to improve reconstruction fidelity and downstream SpeechLLM robustness. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets, 9 open-source and black-box ASR systems, and 4 LALMs demonstrate that T-SemAttack achieves strong transferable attack performance, while the proposed Robust Speech Tokenizer exhibits robustness under high-fidelity reconstruction and downstream tasks. Our code and demo are available at https://wxzyd123.github.io/t-semattack.

title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
abstract: Large language models trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) with verifiable rewards exhibit strong reasoning ability and broad generalization, whereas models trained with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) are often viewed as more prone to memorization and limited transfer. This paper rethinks this distinction through the lens of SFT training data on widely used Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 series models. First, we study the role of data source and show that it is critical: a carefully mixed SFT dataset substantially outperforms data generated solely by a larger model. Second, we study the role of data scale and show that matching the number of correct rollouts between SFT and RL greatly improves SFT generalization, while matching the total rollout budget enables SFT to generalize as well as RL. Combining these two factors further enables SFT to generalize even better than RL. Third, by using LLM annotations to characterize the solution methods in training rollouts, we show that larger datasets cover more tail methods and that these tail methods provide generalizable reasoning signals. Finally, we support these empirical findings theoretically by analyzing the training dynamics of shallow transformers under both RL and SFT.

title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five functional domains and three backbones show that Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities, and remains effective under incremental task arrival.

title: Sophon: A Procedural Diagnostic for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Open-weight Vision-Language Models (VLMs) score 85-94% on spatial benchmarks (BLINK Spatial, What's Up CLEVR) yet collapse to chance on simple geometric questions when object, scene, and texture priors are stripped away. We introduce and open-source Sophon, a procedurally generated diagnostic of paired colored point-cloud stimuli across three coordinate systems (1D linear, 2D Cartesian, 2D polar) and four question types (binary, categorical, comparative, quantitative). Across four open architectures (LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OneVision, Qwen2.5-VL, Idefics3), accuracy clusters at 47-52% while frontier models (Opus 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.4) clear 77-83% and humans reach 84-94%. We use linear probes and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to trace the open-weight failures. Probes of the vision encoder (ViT) and language decoder (LLM) recover Sophon spatial information at 83-85% and 80-86% accuracy, respectively, and the language tower's reasoning circuit answers text-only controls (point clouds as sets of coordinates) at +40 pp over visual stimuli. Language tower per-layer attention attribution localizes visual integration to mid-stack layers. At readout, models elevate the correct answer-set tokens but select among them randomly. We localize the mechanism by tuning individual and grouped components across every architecture's stack, including the vision tower (ViT workspace and reader), the projector, and the language tower (LLM workspace and reader). These experiments demonstrate that this mid-stack workspace holds circuitry capable of organizing the spatial signal so that the frozen reader can decode it. LoRA fine-tuning adjusts that circuitry such that 7B-class VLMs answer Sophon spatial reasoning questions at frontier aggregate accuracy. This work suggests that these models do not have a capability gap for spatial reasoning but suffer from a routing bottleneck that targeted fine-tuning repairs.

title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
abstract: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
abstract: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/

title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
abstract: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs. This is unrealistic in many practical settings, where sensor noise or measurement errors are unavoidable. This discrepancy between model assumptions and real-world data can significantly degrade prediction quality and uncertainty estimates. We introduce Denoising Neural Processes (DnNPs), a principled extension of the NP framework that explicitly models input uncertainty. We train DnNPs via variational inference. DnNPs jointly learn to denoise corrupted inputs and perform meta-learning, making them robust to noisy training data. We demonstrate DnNPs' effectiveness on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing consistent improvements in prediction and uncertainty quantification compared to standard NPs. On PM2.5 spatial interpolation from real-world air quality sensors, DnNP reduces RMSE by up to 30% and NLL by up to 73% relative to standard NPs. We also provide theoretical grounding: we show that the Bayes-optimal predictor under noisy inputs belongs to the DnNP model class, and that plug-in models with fixed observation variance incur an irreducible KL divergence gap that DnNP provably avoids.

title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models
abstract: Concept-based explanations in neural models are important for the development, certification, and adoption of autonomous systems. Yet, interpretability remains correlational. Without methods to guide and quantify causal relationships between explanations, a concept explanation can be provided without being necessary or sufficient for the observed output thereby appearing correct while misleading. We introduce Causal Concept Wrapper Network (CCW-Net), the first use of interventional mediation analysis from fields such as economics, medicine, and epidemiology as a training objective to align causal effects of concept-based explanations with a model's output. We further apply mediation analysis as an evaluation tool to quantify, per concept label combination, how much of any model's output is causally attributable to each concept explanation. As a training objective, CCW-Net shapes a model's concept representations such that they are both necessary and sufficient for the outputs they are credited with and independent of other concepts' contributions. Counterfactual concept representations anchor a set of causal alignment criteria: necessity, sufficiency, and independence. Necessity drives irrelevant concept effects toward zero, sufficiency ensures relevant concept representations fully reconstruct a model's output, and independence enforces the total effect decomposes linearly across concepts. We evaluate CCW-Net across aircraft control, driving, and image classification. CCW-Net provides a step toward concept-based explanations that are not merely interpretable, but quantifiably causal, supporting safer evaluation, certification, and deployment of transparent and trustworthy neural models.

title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state. A recurrent backbone computes its prediction from two inputs: the observed context window and the initial recurrent state. In practice only the first is utilised and the initial state is unused by convention. We ask whether the initial state can be utilised in recurrent TSFMs. Using the xLSTM-based zero-shot forecaster TiRex as a case study, we freeze the backbone and train only a small head that writes a context vector into the initial state, so that any change in accuracy is attributable to the injected state rather than to adapted weights. A spectral summary of the input window, learned once and applied unchanged to every series, lowers mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175%, with every seed improving, which neither a parameter-matched LoRA adapter nor a learnable static state reproduces. An embedding of text attached to each series, evaluated on six MoTime datasets, reveals two roles for the state. As a per-dataset adaptation surface, a static state lowers MASE by 0.04-6.96% of the zero-shot baseline (8-70% of the gain of full fine-tuning). As a channel for exogenous information, the text-conditioned state lowers it by a further 0.15-0.41% of the zero-shot baseline on four of six datasets and, combined with a LoRA adapter, exceeds full fine-tuning, which has no access to the text, on one of them. In TiRex, the effect concentrates in the mLSTM blocks and is strongest at short context. The results are preliminary and the improvements small, but they point to the initial state as a direction for further research.

title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Pooling-Induced Substructures
abstract: Hierarchical graph-level tasks that require reasoning over substructures that extend beyond local neighborhoods are posing challenges for standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). While graph pooling aims to address this by coarsening graphs into hierarchical representations, existing methods often fail to explicitly preserve the substructures they induce, leading to inconsistent empirical performance. Moreover, evaluating such approaches remains challenging due to the lack of benchmarks with explicit hierarchical structure. We propose Pooled-Substructure-Aware GNNs, an approach to graph pooling that explicitly preserves and processes substructures uncovered by structure-based pooling schemes. We show that this design enhances the expressive power of pooling-based GNNs in the sense of the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) test. To enable principled evaluation, we introduce two new synthetic datasets with controllable hierarchical structure and propose a metric to characterize the prevalence of hierarchical patterns in real-world graph-level benchmarks. On tasks with relevant hierarchical structure, our approach outperforms matched pooling baselines, while remaining competitive on structurally simpler benchmarks. Code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/lsbicego/PSA-GNN/.

title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that translates terminal feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment. PMR decomposes evaluation into a universal layer capturing cross-persona failure patterns and a per-user adaptive layer modeling individual traits as a specialized delta over the universal baseline. Through \textbf{Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment}, PMR redistributes credit at the token level, selectively amplifying validated decisions on successful trajectories while falling back to standard policy optimization on failed ones to avoid unreliable attribution. The rubric and memory policy \textbf{co-evolve} in a closed loop with anti-circularity guarantees. Crucially, PMR incurs zero inference overhead, operating without any rubric or external judge during deployment. Extensive experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains over strong memory-augmented baselines.

title: LUMIR: Decoupled Multimodal Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Data for Next-POI Recommendation
abstract: As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). An interaction-aware fusion mechanism is then designed to model cross-modal interactions, while sequential signals are incorporated as a structural constraint to guide representation learning. To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/wzehui/LUMIR.

title: Data Quality Challenges in Multimodal Tourism Recommender Systems
abstract: Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. However, the quality of the underlying multimodal data (e.g. data from social media platforms) has received limited attention so far. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. We outline future directions such as quality-aware fusion, structured and controlled LLM-based content generation to reduce hallucinations, and user group differentiation to improve the robustness and reliability of multimodal recommendation systems.

title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.

title: Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems
abstract: This paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding problems beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions. To this end, we introduce both a novel cocoercivity-type condition and a relaxed Lipschitz continuity condition, and derive convergence of deterministic and stochastic methods under these generalized conditions. For isotropic preconditioners, the resulting algorithms can be interpreted as variable-stepsize variants of classical methods, extending recent analyses based on $(L_0, L_1)$-type growth conditions while allowing simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. We also show that the framework naturally handles variational inequalities through weak Minty-type arguments. Finally, we study the associated continuous-time dynamics and derive a variational and optimal control interpretation of the preconditioned flow. Overall, the results show that dual-space preconditioning provides a flexible mechanism for designing and analyzing operator methods beyond the standard Euclidean Lipschitz setting.

title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

title: Where to Approximate in Neurosymbolic Inference?
abstract: Probabilistic neurosymbolic methods rely on weighted model counting (WMC) to combine neural predictors with symbolic constraints. Exact WMC is #P-hard and typically scales poorly, so many methods resort to approximations. By unifying existing approaches under a three-step bottom-up approximate compilation pipeline, we study where approximation budget is best allocated. Inspired by tensor networks, we instantiate two steps with tensor train decompositions and derive new pipelines that exactly multiply approximated factors and recompress their products via SVD- or interpolation-based schemes. Across six tasks in Sudoku, arithmetic reasoning, and scene understanding, and across increasing problem sizes, our pipelines produce WMC estimates orders-of-magnitude more accurate than prior methods. This translates into stronger downstream learning on tasks where reasoning relies on tight interactions between symbolic factors, where cruder approximations ignore these dependencies. Our pipelines open novel design space for effective approximate compilation of challenging probabilistic reasoning tasks.

title: Plug-and-Play ADMM for Inverse Problems with Flow Matching Denoiser
abstract: Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods with generative priors have achieved strong performance in inverse problems, with recent flow matching models enabling fast and scalable reconstruction. However, a key challenge in PnP methods is maintaining consistency between data fidelity updates and the learned generative prior, as data-consistency steps can move iterates away from the flow trajectory. We propose an ADMM-based PnP framework for flow matching priors that enforces stronger consistency between the measurement model and the prior through auxiliary variables and dual updates. In addition, we introduce a trajectory correction mechanism that restores consistency with the flow via a combination of deterministic and stochastic projections. Our method provides a more principled integration of flow priors within PnP frameworks, achieving high-quality reconstructions with reduced computational cost.

title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at https://github.com/buraksusam/AutoManifold_NeurIPS2026.

title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
abstract: Privacy concerns have been raised in Large Language Models (LLM) inference when models are deployed in Cloud Service Providers (CSP). Homomorphic encryption (HE) offers a promising solution by enabling secure inference directly over encrypted inputs. However, the high computational overhead of HE remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose MOAI, an efficient HE-based, non-interactive framework for secure transformer inference. MOAI gains significant efficiency improvement from: (1) a novel evaluation flow that combines column and diagonal packing with consistent strategies across all layers, eliminating expensive format conversions. (2) rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that significantly reduce the number of costly HE rotations, removing 2,448 HE rotations in BERT-base inference. (3) Column packing removes rotations in plaintext-ciphertext matrix multiplications and interleaved batching further reduces the rotations in ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplications. MOAI uses at least 1.7x fewer HE rotations compared to the state-of-the-art works across all matrix multiplications of BERT-base. As a result, we achieve a $52.8 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to the state-of-the-art HE-based non-interactive secure transformer inference, THOR (Moon et al., CCS 25). We then apply MOAI on the Powerformer's framework and achieve a $55.7 \%$ reduction in evaluation time compared to Powerformer (Park et al., ACL 25), which approximates Softmax and LayerNorm with simpler functions in transformer and proposes HE-based non-interactive transformer inference. We report an amortized time of 2.36 minutes per input on a single GPU environment. We show the extendibility by applying MOAI in LLaMA-3-8B. Our implementation is publicly available as open source.

title: Curriculum proof repair with learned counterexamples
abstract: Language models (LMs) have substantially lowered the barrier to applying formal verification for building reliable and secure software. Existing approaches commonly follow the verifier-in-the-loop paradigm, but the verifier often provides only coarse, binary pass/fail feedback, which offers little actionable signal on how the proof should be repaired. Recent work shows that counterexamples provide more actionable feedback by grounding proof failures in concrete program states, but generating useful ones at inference time requires costly iterative refinement. We present TopoVerus, an LM-based framework for Verus proof repair that internalizes counterexample-guided diagnosis as a model capability, producing useful counterexamples in a single pass. Our key insight is to train counterexample generation not as a standalone validation task, but as a data-driven diagnostic objective: a counterexample is useful when conditioning on it helps the model produce a safe, verifier-passing proof. Given a failed Verus proof and verifier error, TopoVerus generates a structured source-level counterexample, repair rationale, and repaired proof in one trajectory, optimized with reinforcement learning from Verus feedback and a proof-code safety gate. To guide the order of invariant repairs, TopoVerus introduces a curriculum with a topological graph reward based on invariant dependencies derived from inductiveness tests, which encourages counterexample generation to follow the same topological order. Across seven Verus benchmarks with 471 problems, TopoVerus achieves 61.6%/72.2% weighted-average Safe-Pass@1/Safe-Pass@3, outperforming the strongest baseline, Claude Sonnet 4.5, by 5.7/6.3 points. We also show that TopoVerus's learned counterexamples can directly augment the reasoning of existing LM-based proof repair approaches, improving their success rate by 64.3% compared to chain-of-thought diagnostics.

title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local perception, action-conditioned transitions, presentation stability, representation exchangeability, and Full-CF causal discrimination. Our diagnostic evaluations reveal heterogeneous failure modes, including sensitivity to evidence presentation and encoding, low activation on successful trajectories, and weak paired counterfactual discrimination. Perception-controlled analyses further indicate that visual grounding and objective recovery are substantial, model-dependent bottlenecks. These results motivate jointly reporting correctness, presentation stability, and causal sensitivity instead of relying on a single score.

title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
abstract: Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains untested. In a separate case500 training experiment, augmentation lowers transformed-view error in three of four models and median discrepancy and constraint-violation P95 in all four. These benefits depend on the training protocol: some relations worsen, and every evaluated prediction remains AC infeasible. A GPU/CPU eigensolver mismatch accounts for most of the large raw-Laplacian-baseline gain. We recommend reporting representation consistency alongside accuracy, feasibility, and cost. These results establish neither deployment readiness nor universal invariance.

title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are commonly evaluated by variance explained and ablation damage. We show how massive activations undermine both evaluations, and propose a correction. Massive activations cause up to 99.9% of activation variance to lie along the first principal component (PC1). Because the PC1 component has no unique sparse decomposition, each SAE run rebuilds it from a different set of features. These features dominate importance rankings: an average of 47 of the 50 most important features are unmatched in a separate run, compared with about 27 of a random 50. A dictionary can also report 99.96% of variance explained while leaving 33% of the variance outside PC1 unexplained. We bypass PC1 by training the SAE on activations with PC1 removed, then adding PC1 to the reconstruction. In affected models, the top-50 feature sharing rate rises from 4-39.5% to 73-99.5%. At the same TopK sparsity, the resulting SAE degrades the model up to 44% less and reduces content reconstruction error by up to 33.9%.

title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
abstract: Nonlinear state space models are typically evaluated sequentially, limiting their ability to exploit modern parallel hardware. Recent work has shown that state space models can be evaluated in parallel by reformulating evaluation as a root-finding problem, which can be solved with a parallel form of Newton's method. However, exact Newton methods require expensive multiplication of dense Jacobian matrices, and quasi-Newton methods based on diagonal approximations, while more scalable, are often slow to converge because they neglect interactions across state dimensions. We introduce a novel quasi-Newton approach based on Broyden's method, which captures coupling terms with diagonal-plus-low-rank approximations to blocks of the Jacobian. We construct the approximations from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation while retaining the favorable scaling of diagonal approximations and remaining compatible with parallel scan through rank compression. We prove finite-step recovery of the exact trajectory under the compressed scan, and show that convergence is tracked by the compression error and by the block approximation error along the current trajectory error, rather than in spectral norm. Empirically, we show that our method is advantageous when interactions are approximately low rank or when Jacobian evaluation is expensive: on low-rank RNNs, parallel MCMC algorithms, and denoising diffusion models, it converges in fewer iterations than other quasi-Newton methods and is the fastest parallel method when Jacobian evaluation is expensive or state dimensions are large.

title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
abstract: Compositional generalization is an important form of out-of-distribution generalization, defined as the ability to train on some combinations of modules (e.g., functions such as sort, filter) and then generalize to unseen combinations. Despite substantial empirical work evaluating compositional generalization in transformers, findings have been inconsistent because evaluations were often conducted on a limited set of train-test splits, defined in an ad hoc manner. Through a systematic evaluation, we identify two key aspects of the train-test distribution that strongly affect performance: composition equivalence and module coverage. We show that the apparent performance of direct models (trained only on final outputs) results primarily from exploiting composition equivalences, meaning different sequences of modules that reduce to identical end-to-end functions. When benchmarks eliminate these equivalences, performance drops significantly, showing their inability to generalize to compositions of known modules that produce novel end-to-end functions. We further demonstrate that performance degrades monotonically as module coverage shifts increase (when modules appear in different contexts between train and test), affecting both direct and step-by-step models (trained on intermediate and final outputs).
